claims.text: TOR-TILD currently uses EAM reference potentials.
EAM references inadequately represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid.
A new potential should be developed to incorporate many-body interactions more effectively.
The new potential will represent atomic configurations in multicomponent high-entropy alloys better than the EAM references.
More effective treatment of many-body interactions will capture the complex interactions and configurations of the ab initio liquid more accurately.
More accurate capture of liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch could be reduced by approximately an order of magnitude.
The proposed potential is applicable to both solid and liquid multicomponent high-entropy alloys near high melting temperatures.
The applicable alloys are limited to high-entropy compositions containing multiple elements.
The magnitude of path-mismatch reduction depends on the particular compositions and configurations tested.
The new potential should be benchmarked against TOR-TILD EAM references over a range of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The benchmark will measure thermodynamic-integration path lengths and free-energy differences obtained with the two reference approaches.
Failure to achieve a significant reduction in path mismatch relative to the EAM references will falsify the hypothesis.
